title: What exhaustion reaches, and what lies outside it — 8 machine-checked theorems and how they are bound
description:
What exhaustion reaches, and what lies outside it. 8 machine-checked theorems from the Lean 4 source file src/proof/reach.lean, by Tsvetan Rouschev, licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Lean 4 is a proof checker: a theorem it accepts has been checked by its kernel, not argued in prose. 4 are checked case by case over a stated finite domain (by decide). 4 are proved for every value, on the standard axioms only (propext, Quot.sound; the verifier refuses any other). Every theorem listed is sealed live in the deposit's ledger, where a withdrawal is marked in place; 63 earlier rows removed on 2026-08-09 are listed in src/proof/revoked.json.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used here in a precise, non-quantum sense: theorems are bound when they derive from shared definitions (section 1), when their files import one another (section 2), and when their content-addressed receipts fold into one address that changes if any one of them changes (section 3). It is correlation by derivation; no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 1 definition is used by two or more theorems, binding 6 pairs; the theorems fall into 5 strands, the largest of 4. Most binding: bounds (4). 4 theorems name no definition of the file and stand on their own statement.

2 · Imports. Built on: no other cluster. Built on it: no other cluster. Checking this cluster needs 1 file: src/proof/reach.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 8 sealed receipts fold to fa9dcd6d-5209-8845-b954-584568daaac6. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed when this record was generated. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (0, 6, 2, 2, 8, 4, 4). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs counted from this cluster's theorems' seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: ledgerclaims.lean (3 observed, 0.65 expected, lift 4.65), coin.lean (4 observed, 0.97 expected, lift 4.13), elementary.lean (7 observed, 2.9 expected, lift 2.41). A best lift is the largest of about 32 small ratios, so chance alone gives a typical best lift of 3.38 here (the median over 200 seeded reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to); one at least as high as this cluster's arose in 13.5% of them — consistent with chance. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 15.5; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.45. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). These figures are as of commit f5589aa93919 (2026-09-15), over 695 points; a new seal anywhere moves them.

Prior art. That no finite set contains every natural number is Euclid's argument in form and is as old as mathematics; the deposit claims none of it. What is its own here is the decision over its OWN bounds, and the statement of where that decision stops. Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json (main branch). No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. exhaustion_never_reaches_its_own_bound — bounds.all (fun n => (List.range n).length == n && ¬ (List.range n).contains n) record
  2. the_successor_of_every_bound_lies_outside — bounds.all (fun n => ¬ (List.range n).contains (n + 1)) record
  3. doubling_the_domain_leaves_the_same_hole — bounds.all (fun n => ¬ (List.range (2 * n)).contains (2 * n)) record
  4. the_successor_leaves_every_domain_and_the_predecessor_returns — (bounds ++ [largestDomainHere]).all (fun n => n + 1 > n && (n + 1) - 1 == n && (n + 1) % 2 != n % 2) record
  5. the_predecessor_returns_every_successor — ∀ n : Nat, (n + 1) - 1 = n record
  6. exhaustion_never_reaches_its_own_bound_for_every_n — ∀ n : Nat, (List.range n).length = n ∧ n ∉ List.range n record
  7. the_successor_of_every_bound_lies_outside_for_every_n — ∀ n : Nat, n + 1 ∉ List.range n record
  8. doubling_the_domain_leaves_the_same_hole_for_every_n — ∀ n : Nat, 2 * n ∉ List.range (2 * n) record

Recompute. Clone https://github.com/ceccec/millennium-solutions at commit f5589aa93919 and run npm ci && npm run lean, which checks every Lean file in dependency order. This record was generated by scripts/clusters.ts from the source and the ledger.
